{"answer": "The date 1900-02-29 is valid in the Julian calendar but invalid in the Gregorian calendar. In Julian, 1900 is divisible by 4, so it is a leap year. In Gregorian, 1900 is a century year not divisible by 400, so it is not a leap year. Thus, February 29, 1900, does not exist in Gregorian. The importer should ask for the calendar convention, not silently normalize it. [EVAL-H03-S1]", "citations": ["EVAL-H03-S1"], "actions": [], "grounding": [{"sourceId": "EVAL-H03-S1", "quote": "Julian years divisible by 4 are leap years. Gregorian years divisible by 4 are leap years except century years not divisible by 400.", "claim": "February 29, 1900, is valid in Julian but not in Gregorian."}]}
